# Structure output examples

Examples use a fictional accounting firm. Replace with the user's real audiences and content.

## Audiences and top tasks

| Audience | Top tasks | Value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Small business owners | Understand services, see prices, book a call | High |
| Existing clients | Upload documents, contact their accountant | High |
| Job seekers | See open roles, apply | Low |

## Sitemap

```text
/                         Home
/services                 Services overview
  /services/bookkeeping   Bookkeeping
  /services/tax-filing    Tax filing
/pricing                  Pricing
/about                    About us
/contact                  Contact and booking
/client-portal            Client sign-in (utility)
/careers                  Careers (footer)
```

## Navigation

- Primary: Services, Pricing, About, Contact.
- Utility: Client sign-in.
- Footer: Careers, Privacy policy, Terms.
- Mobile: primary items in a menu button; "Book a call" stays visible.

## User flow: book a call

1. Lands on Home from search.
2. Opens Services, then Bookkeeping.
3. Checks Pricing.
4. Uses the "Book a call" button on Pricing.
5. Completes the booking form on Contact. Possible drop-off: long form; keep to 4 fields.

## Page content hierarchy: Pricing

- Purpose: help an owner choose a plan.
- Primary action: book a call for the chosen plan.
- Sections: plan comparison, what is included, common questions, call to action.
